clue.text: Cult leader on drugs quietly tries to get sorted out

parts.note: someone on drugs is high
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: things sorted out are rearranged, so the letters of tries are reordered

explanation.surface: A cult's leader, high on drugs, quietly tries to get his life in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges TRIES into RIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A high priest is the chief religious official of a sect, so a cult leader.

clue.text: Part of wheel clamp oddly below centre

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means the second piece is written under the first

parts.note: a hub is a centre of activity

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of the word clamp

explanation.surface: A wheel clamp fitted strangely low, beneath the middle of the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes C, A, P from CLAMP; 'below' puts them under HUB in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hubcap is the metal disc covering the centre of a car wheel, a component of it.

clue.text: Law must be broken in cheerful port city

indicators.note: in says the scrambled piece goes inside the word for cheerful

parts.note: gay in its older sense means cheerful

indicators.note: a word that is broken is smashed and put back together differently, so the letters of law are reordered

explanation.surface: A happy port city where the law must be broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be broken' turns LAW into ALW, which goes 'in' GAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway is a harbour city on the west coast of Ireland.

clue.text: Material supplied for cast following break

definitions.text: Material supplied for cast following break

parts.words: Material supplied for cast following break
parts.note: the cast is for a broken limb, not actors, and the material used to make it is a white powder that sets hard when mixed with water

explanation.surface: Reads like costumes or scripts handed to a theatre cast after the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' and 'break' suggest the stage (a cast, a break between acts), but it is a fracture set in a plaster cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster of Paris is the gypsum compound used to make rigid casts for broken bones.

clue.text: Quickly seeing one replaced by a name, spellbound

indicators.note: replaced by says one piece is swapped out for another inside the phrase meaning quickly

parts.note: in a trice means very quickly
I is the Roman numeral for one
A as written, plus N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone quickly seeing a single item swapped for a name, as if enchanted.
explanation.walkthrough: IN A TRICE, swapping its second I for AN, gives IN A TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a trance is held motionless as if under a spell.

clue.text: Fly high crossing line of the sun

indicators.note: crossing here means spanning around, so the word for flying high encloses the line

parts.note: to soar is to fly high

explanation.surface: Something flying high across the line of the sun, like Icarus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts L inside SOAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar is the adjective relating to the sun.

clue.text: Request that may see enjoyment cut by half?

indicators.note: cutting a word by half keeps only its first half, four of its eight letters

parts.note: pleasure means enjoyment

explanation.surface: A request that might see someone's fun cut in half.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal or entreaty, a request.

clue.text: Blinks, surprised about a medium woollen cloth

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the other pieces
surprised hints at something thrown into disorder, so the letters of blinks are rearranged

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: Someone blinks in surprise at a medium-sized woollen garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprised' turns BLINKS into LBSKIN; 'about' wraps it round A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambskin is the fleece-covered hide of a lamb, or a fabric made to resemble it.

clue.text: Sailor — isn't he drunk, having drunk this?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common term for a sailor

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about, so isn't he is rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a sailor is drunk after drinking this spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ISNT HE into SINTHE. The definition is 'this', what the sailor has drunk, so the whole clue points to the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green liqueur, the thing a drunken sailor might have downed.

clue.text: Orders may be transmitted through this mountain HQ

definitions.text: Orders may be transmitted through this mountain HQ

parts.words: Orders may be transmitted through this mountain HQ
parts.note: orders pass down a hierarchy; a mountain range is a chain, and a headquarters is a command, so the clue sketches a command post in a range of peaks

explanation.surface: A military headquarters high in the mountains relaying orders.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain of mountains and a command base combine to give the military hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of command is the line of authority through which instructions pass downward.

clue.text: Revolutionary American flag and tree

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the combined pieces read backwards

parts.note: a flag is a flagstone, a paving slab

explanation.surface: A revolutionary American flag hoisted beside a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is a paving stone, not a banner. A + SLAB read backwards gives the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a tropical American tree yielding very light wood.

clue.text: Awkward seeing husband lodging in small but poor surroundings

indicators.note: lodging in means staying inside, so one piece sits within the rearranged letters
poor suggests something badly made, so the letters of small but are reformed

explanation.surface: A husband lodging in shabby, cramped surroundings feels uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns SMALL BUT into ALLTUMBS; H goes inside ('lodging in' ... 'surroundings').
explanation.definitionFit: Being all thumbs is an idiom for being clumsy with the hands.

clue.text: Sort of plug more suitable after promotion

indicators.note: after places the word for more suitable following the promotion

parts.note: an ad promotes a product
apter is the comparative of apt, suitable

explanation.surface: A plug that seems a better fit after being advertised.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter plug lets a device fit a socket of a different kind.

clue.text: Endure insinuations about controls?

indicators.note: about here means found in, so the answer lies inside the run of letters endure insinuations

explanation.surface: Putting up with insinuations about one's controls.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in endu-REINSIN-uations. The question mark flags that 'controls' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or keep in check, as with a horse's reins.

clue.text: Coat found by two Europeans

definitions.meaning: A glossy shellac finish applied to wood
a French person and a Polish person

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two nationalities side by side, the phrase is a pair of Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is a varnish-like coating for furniture.

clue.text: Dispute rumour accepted by people with wealth

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the rumour goes inside the word for the wealthy

parts.note: the haves are the well-off, as in haves and have-nots
word means news or rumour, as in word has it

explanation.surface: Rich people take in gossip and start quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The haves' is the idiom for the wealthy, as opposed to the have-nots.
explanation.definitionFit: To have words with someone is an idiom for to argue with them.

clue.text: Baffled and sadly unfocussed with no American

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone baffled and miserably out of focus, without the American.
explanation.walkthrough: Take US ('with no American') from UNFOCUSSED and 'sadly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confused means being bewildered, unable to understand.

clue.text: Offer and pay for a case of red that's average

parts.note: to stand can mean offer (stand for office) and pay for (stand someone a drink)

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, here the first and last of red

explanation.surface: Someone offers to buy a case of red wine of ordinary quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes R and D from RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard can mean normal or usual, of ordinary quality.

clue.text: Switching vote if course not working

indicators.note: switching means changing places, so the letters of vote if course are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changing one's vote if the course of events changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of service describes a machine or vehicle that is unavailable or broken.

clue.text: Star's key broadcast

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: A celebrity's key programme being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star's' reads as 'Star is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Climb when cold and finish

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
end means finish

explanation.surface: Instructions to climb while it is cold and then stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to go upward, scaling a slope or stairs, is both to climb and the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Flyer's collapse, having swallowed insect

indicators.note: having swallowed means taking something inside, so the insect goes within the word for collapse

parts.note: fail means collapse or break down
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bird collapses after swallowing a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer's' reads as 'Flyer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a pigeon or flycatcher with a fan-shaped tail, a bird.

clue.text: Language used in baffling organisers

indicators.note: used in says the answer is contained within the letters of baffling organisers

explanation.surface: Organisers baffling people with jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across baff-LING O-rganisers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language or specialist jargon.

clue.text: Women once used these cunning ploys to snare politician

indicators.note: to snare means to catch and hold, so the politician is trapped inside the word for ploys

parts.note: wiles are cunning tricks
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Women of old using crafty tricks to trap a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Women once used these' is fair because the headdress is now historical, worn chiefly by some nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimples were cloth headdresses worn by medieval women and still by some nuns.

clue.text: Stop here essentially for this merchant

parts.note: a station is a stop on a railway line

indicators.note: essentially points to the heart of a word, so the middle letters of here are taken

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper told to stop here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes ER from the middle of HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a dealer selling paper, pens and office supplies.

clue.text: Stone barrier on the west of Alcatraz

indicators.note: on a map the west is the left side, so the west of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: A stone barrier on the western side of the prison island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'west of Alcatraz' is its first letter, A, placed on the west (left) of GATE in this across entry. Alcatraz is a former prison island in San Francisco Bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Useless son finds clothes

parts.note: a dud is something useless; the noun stands in for the adjective in the surface

explanation.surface: A good-for-nothing son finds some clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Duds is informal slang for clothes.

clue.text: Gave thought to Tory team on the left

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
a side is a sports team
red describes the political left

explanation.surface: Considering a Conservative team that sits on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are Britain's Conservatives; a Tory side on the left is the political joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To have considered something is to have thought about it carefully.
